subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is a student visa?
option_a: Permission to enter a country to study
explanation: A student visa lets you enter and stay in another country for full-time study.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which document do you usually need FIRST before applying for a student visa?
option_b: An admission or offer letter from a school
explanation: Almost every country asks for proof that a recognised school has accepted you.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What does 'proof of funds' mean?
option_c: Evidence you have enough money for fees and living costs
explanation: Embassies check you can pay for your studies and life without relying on illegal work.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which document must be valid for travel abroad?
explanation: Many countries want your passport to stay valid for some months beyond your planned stay.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What are 'biometrics' in a visa application?
option_a: Fingerprints and a photo of your face
explanation: Biometrics prove your identity and are collected at visa centres or by official apps.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which is the SAFEST place to check visa rules?
explanation: Rules and fees change often, so official sites have the latest information.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What should you NEVER submit with a visa application?
explanation: Fake documents can lead to refusal and even a ban from applying again.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What does IELTS mainly test?
explanation: IELTS, TOEFL and PTE are common English tests accepted for study visas.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Why do many countries ask for health insurance for students?
option_a: To cover medical costs during your stay
explanation: Medical treatment abroad can be very expensive, so insurance is often compulsory.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is an 'SOP' often asked for in study applications?
explanation: An SOP explains why you chose the course and how it fits your future plans.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is a visa interview?
option_c: A meeting where an officer asks about your study plans
explanation: Officers check that you are a genuine student with clear plans and funds.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What does 'genuine student' mean to a visa officer?
option_d: Your main purpose is really to study
explanation: Countries like Australia formally test whether applicants truly intend to study.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Who usually issues the admission letter?
explanation: Schools issue offers; the government immigration department issues the visa.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is an education loan 'sanction letter'?
option_b: A bank letter confirming your loan is approved
explanation: Many embassies accept loan sanction letters as part of your proof of funds.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which of these is usually NOT a reason for visa refusal?
explanation: Common refusal reasons are weak finances, unclear plans and false information.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: When should you usually start your visa process?
option_d: Several months before the course starts
explanation: Processing can take weeks or months, so early applications are safer.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What does 'apostille' on a document mean?
option_a: An official certificate confirming the document is genuine for use abroad
explanation: Countries in the Hague Apostille Convention accept apostilled documents from each other.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is a 'police clearance certificate'?
option_b: A document showing you have no criminal record
explanation: Some countries ask for police or character certificates with study visas.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: If an agent says they can 'guarantee' your visa, what should you think?
option_c: Be careful – no one can guarantee a visa
explanation: Only the government decides visas; guarantees are a common sign of fraud.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What does a 'scholarship letter' help prove?
option_d: That some or all of your costs are paid
explanation: Scholarships count as financial support in most visa applications.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Why is it important that your name is spelled the same on all documents?
option_a: Mismatches can delay or refuse your visa
explanation: Officers compare passport, admission and visa forms; differences cause problems.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is the main student visa for academic study in the USA?
explanation: F-1 is for academic study; M-1 is for vocational courses and J-1 for exchanges.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which form does a US school issue to an F-1 student?
explanation: The I-20 is the Certificate of Eligibility for Nonimmigrant Student Status.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is the DS-160?
option_d: The online US nonimmigrant visa application form
explanation: You fill in the DS-160 online before booking your visa interview.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: How much is the SEVIS I-901 fee for most F-1 students in 2026?
explanation: The SEVIS fee is paid at fmjfee.com and the receipt is taken to the interview.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: How much is the US student visa (MRV) application fee in 2026?
explanation: Together with the SEVIS fee, government fees for an F-1 total about US$535.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: In the UK, what is the CAS?
explanation: Your licensed UK sponsor gives you a CAS number to use in your visa application.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: How many points does a UK Student visa applicant need?
explanation: 50 points for the CAS, 10 for money and 10 for English.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: For a UK Student visa, money must be held for how many days in a row?
explanation: The 28-day period must end within 31 days of the visa application date.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is the UK monthly living-cost amount for students studying in London?
explanation: Outside London the amount is £1,171 per month, counted for up to 9 months.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Up to how many months of living costs must UK Student visa applicants show?
explanation: The UK counts maintenance for up to 9 months, whatever the course length.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: How early can you apply for a UK Student visa from outside the UK?
option_d: Up to 6 months before the course
explanation: GOV.UK lets you apply up to six months before your course start date.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What extra health payment do most UK visa applicants make?
explanation: The IHS gives access to the UK's National Health Service during your stay.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is the usual English level needed for UK degree-level study visas?
explanation: B2 is upper-intermediate; universities may set higher scores.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: In Canada, what is a DLI?
explanation: Only DLIs can host international students on a study permit.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which Canadian department issues study permits?
explanation: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada handles study permits.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What letter do most Canadian study permit applicants need from the province?
explanation: Provinces issue PALs within the national study permit cap.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: From 1 January 2026, who no longer needs a PAL in Canada?
option_b: Master's and PhD students at public institutions
explanation: This exemption started on 1 January 2026 for graduate students at public DLIs.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Students going to Quebec need which extra certificate?
explanation: Quebec selects its own international students through the CAQ.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: From 1 September 2026, how much must a single applicant outside Quebec show for living costs?
explanation: This is in addition to first-year tuition and travel costs.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Where is a Canadian study permit actually issued after approval?
option_a: At the port of entry in Canada
explanation: Approved students get a letter to show the border officer, who issues the permit.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which countries need you to give biometrics for study visas?
option_b: Many countries, including the UK, Canada and Ireland
explanation: Biometrics help confirm identity and are now very common.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is Australia's main student visa called?
explanation: Subclass 485 is the post-study Temporary Graduate visa, not the student visa.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What document proves enrolment for an Australian student visa?
explanation: You cannot lodge a subclass 500 application without a valid CoE.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is OSHC in Australia?
explanation: OSHC is compulsory health insurance for international students.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Where do you apply online for an Australian student visa?
explanation: ImmiAccount is the Department of Home Affairs online system.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What did Australia's student visa charge rise to on 1 July 2026?
explanation: It rose from AUD 2,000, after rising from AUD 1,600 in 2025.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: How many hours can student visa holders in Australia work during study periods?
explanation: Work is limited during study periods so that study stays the main purpose.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Courses for Australian student visas must be on which register?
explanation: CRICOS lists institutions and courses approved for overseas students.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is the main New Zealand visa for international students paying fees?
explanation: It can be granted for up to 4 years.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: How much must a New Zealand student show for a year of living costs?
explanation: For courses under a year, it is NZD 1,667 per month.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: How many hours a week can most student visa holders in New Zealand work during study (since Nov 2025)?
explanation: The limit rose from 20 to 25 hours on 3 November 2025.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: For Ireland, courses for non-EU students must be on which list?
option_a: ILEP – Interim List of Eligible Programmes
explanation: Only courses on the ILEP qualify for student permission in Ireland.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which online system is used to apply for an Irish study visa?
explanation: AVATS is Ireland's online visa application system.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: How much must students show for a course longer than 8 months in Ireland?
explanation: This applies to both visa-required and non-visa-required students since 30 June 2025.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which student immigration stamp do students register for in Ireland?
explanation: Stamp 2 allows part-time work: 20 hours in term and 40 in holidays.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is a German 'Sperrkonto'?
option_a: A blocked bank account for proof of funds
explanation: You can only withdraw a fixed amount each month from a blocked account.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: How much must be in a German blocked account for one year in 2026?
explanation: It is released at €992 per month.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What must you do soon after arriving in Germany?
explanation: Address registration is needed before you get your residence permit.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which certificate do Indian students usually need before a German student visa?
explanation: The Academic Evaluation Centre (APS) checks the authenticity of academic documents.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: How many full days a year can students work in Germany?
explanation: Students can also take jobs at the university under separate rules.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Why is Germany popular despite needing a blocked account?
option_b: Many public universities charge little or no tuition
explanation: Most German public universities charge only a small semester contribution.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What must the duration of OSHC in Australia cover?
explanation: Keeping valid OSHC is a condition of the student visa.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is the French long-stay student visa called?
explanation: VLS-TS means a long-stay visa equivalent to a residence permit.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which organisation runs the 'Études en France' procedure?
explanation: Students from many countries, including India, must complete it before the visa.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: From 1 August 2026, what monthly resources must French student visa applicants show?
explanation: It rose from €615 and is now linked to the French minimum wage (SMIC).

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Within how long must you validate your French VLS-TS after arrival?
explanation: Validation is done online and makes the visa work as a residence permit.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: How many hours a year can students work in France?
explanation: 964 hours equals about 60% of a full-time working year.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: In the Netherlands, who submits the study residence permit application?
option_a: The university, on the student's behalf
explanation: Dutch law does not allow students to apply for a study permit themselves.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is the Dutch 'MVV'?
explanation: Some nationalities need an MVV to enter, plus the residence permit (VVR).

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which Dutch agency decides residence permits?
explanation: The Immigration and Naturalisation Service (IND) handles visas and permits.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What share of credits must non-EU students in the Netherlands usually earn each year?
explanation: Insufficient study progress can lead to the permit being withdrawn.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What does a Japanese school apply for on your behalf before your visa?
explanation: The CoE is issued by Japan's Immigration Services Agency.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What card do students receive at the airport when entering Japan for study?
explanation: The Residence Card shows your status of residence in Japan.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What do students in Japan need before doing part-time work?
option_c: Permission to Engage in Activity Other Than That Permitted
explanation: Working without this permission can risk your student status.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which agency issues the Singapore Student's Pass?
explanation: The Immigration & Checkpoints Authority handles Student's Pass applications.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is SOLAR in Singapore?
explanation: Students submit eForm 16 through SOLAR after the school registers them.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What letter do successful Student's Pass applicants receive first?
explanation: The IPA is not the pass itself – formalities are completed after arrival.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: How early can a new student arrive in Singapore before the course starts?
explanation: ICA asks students to arrive close to the start date and present the IPA.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is South Korea's main degree student visa?
explanation: D-4 is used for language training; D-2 for degree programmes.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What document does a Korean university issue for the D-2 visa?
explanation: The embassy uses the CoA to process your D-2 visa.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What card must students in Korea register for after arrival?
explanation: The ARC is the identity card for foreign residents in Korea.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What happens to a D-2 visa if a student withdraws from university?
option_a: It turns into a work visa
option_c: It ends and the student must leave
explanation: Student visas depend on staying enrolled and studying.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which country's student visa is called 'Student's Pass'?
explanation: Singapore uses passes issued by ICA rather than a traditional visa label.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which country's student visa uses a points system needing 70 points?
explanation: UK points: CAS 50, finances 10, English 10.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Match: CoE is to Australia as CAS is to…
explanation: Both are enrolment documents from the school used in the visa application.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Match: I-20 is to the USA as CoA is to…
explanation: Each is the school-issued document needed for the student visa.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which country requires a blocked account of €11,904 a year?
explanation: France uses a monthly resources rule; Ireland asks for €10,000.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: In which country must the university, not the student, apply for the study permit?
explanation: Dutch universities act as sponsors and apply to the IND.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which country asks students to complete Études en France first?
explanation: It is managed by Campus France in many countries.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which country has an annual national cap on study permits shared by provinces?
explanation: Provinces issue attestation letters within their share of the cap.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is the UK 'Immigration Health Surcharge' for?
option_d: Access to the NHS during your stay
explanation: Most applicants pay the IHS as part of their visa application.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which test checks if Australian applicants really intend to study?
explanation: It replaced the older GTE requirement in 2024.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is ATAS in the UK?
option_b: A security clearance for certain sensitive subjects
explanation: The Academic Technology Approval Scheme applies to some science and technology courses.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: A UK applicant had £10,000 for 27 days, then 1 day at £9,000. Do they meet the 28-day rule?
option_c: No – the full amount must stay for 28 days in a row
explanation: Any day below the required amount breaks the 28-day period.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which country's living-cost requirement for students is NZD 20,000 per year?
explanation: Australia's figure is AUD 29,710 a year.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which country gives students 48 hours of work per fortnight?
explanation: That is the same as an average of 24 hours a week.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which country allows students 964 hours of work a year?
explanation: Germany instead counts 140 full or 280 half days.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What should you do if a visa rule on a blog differs from the official website?
explanation: Blogs can be out of date; official sites are updated when rules change.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Why do officers check the SOURCE of money, not just the balance?
option_d: To make sure funds are genuine and will stay available
explanation: Sudden unexplained deposits are a common red flag in visa checks.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is a 'visa refusal letter' useful for later?
option_a: Understanding the reasons so you can fix them before reapplying
explanation: Many countries also ask you to declare past refusals honestly.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which document proves you can pay future years' fees in a multi-year course?
option_b: A credible funding plan, such as loans, savings or sponsorship
explanation: New Zealand, for example, says a credible plan for later years strengthens your application.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: Which student permission in Ireland allows 40 hours a week of work?
explanation: During term, the limit is 20 hours a week.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What does 'maintaining status' usually require of international students?
option_d: Staying enrolled full-time and following work limits
explanation: Breaking study or work conditions can lead to losing your visa.

subject: Student Visas & Study Abroad
question: What is the best way to stay safe from visa fraud?
option_a: Apply only through official websites and authorised centres
explanation: Official portals and authorised visa centres are listed on government websites.
